svg.title: Align the change before predicting its coding effect
svg.desc: In a stated5′→3′ first-base coding frame, reference ATGGAATTTTAA groups ATG|GAA|TTT|TAA. Adding A immediately after ATG gives ATGAGAATTTTAA, grouped ATG|AGA|ATT|TTA|A, with the final A explicitly incomplete. A separate illustrative in-frame three-base GCT addition at that codon boundary gives ATG|GCT|GAA|TTT|TAA and preserves later grouping; this example does not imply all insertion boundaries leave adjacent codons unchanged. Specified RNA substitutions GAA→GAG,GAA→GUA,GAA→UAA demonstrate synonymous Glu→Glu,missense Glu→Val and nonsense premature-stop consequences respectively. These are sequence predictions, not guarantees of overall phenotype or universal neutrality of synonymous changes.

g.text: Align the change before predicting its coding effect
Exact reference/insertion teaching sequences are separated from labelled comparison variants.
Coding DNA, 5′→3′, grouping from the stated first-base frame:
Three bases added at a boundary
A one-base insertion shifts later grouping; the final A is an incomplete triplet, not a full codon.
A three-base insertion preserves the downstream frame; boundary and functional effects still matter.
RNA substitutions in a stated translated region: GAA → GAG (Glu → Glu, synonymous);
GAA → GUA (Glu → Val, missense); GAA → UAA (Glu → premature stop, nonsense).
No amino-acid change means the predicted chain is unchanged at that position; RNA effects may remain.
